newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CDL Hotels sees stronger 2nd half profit.
newsitem.headline: CDL Hotels sees stronger 2nd half profit.

text.p: CDL Hotels New Zealand Ltd on Thursday recorded a 40 percent fall in first half profit to NZ$4.8 million from $8.1 million lat year, but said it was condident of a stronger profit in the seond half.

"Barring unforeseen circumstances, the board is expecting a stronger profit in the second half of the year due to seasonality of factors, a higher base of business expected for the new hotels and increased contribution from our subsidiaries," the company said in a statement.

CDL Hotels said the exhaustion of tax losses resulted in a tax provision of $2.559 million this year. This, together with the inclusion in last year's equivalent period of a gain of $1.956 million from the disposal of Hellaby Holdings shares and increased minority interest, resulted in a 40 percent decline in the net profit after tax from the previous corresponding year.
CDL Investments, a 57.4 percent subsidiary, reported a net profit after tax of $3.065 million for the 6 months ending June 30, down from $3.8 million in the correspnding previous period.
"An enhanced contribution is expected from CDL Investments in the second half of 1997 due to timing of project launches," CDL Hotels said.
Kingsgate International Corporation, a 50.74 percent subsidiary, reported a profit of $2.5 million for the six months.
"The board remains positive about the tong-term growth prospects for the tourism sector both in Australia and New Zealand," CDL Hotels said.

"However, the motel market environment will continue to be extremely competitive as new room inventory comes onstream. Consequently, the profit contribution from the two listed subsidiaries will be very important in determining group profitability."
